pages.text:
Aaditya Padte
B.Tech CS
INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
On-campus Hiring:
JPMC uses Code for Good (CFG), a two-day hackathon, to conduct
on-campus hiring every year for summer internships and full-time
positions.
In order to develop tech solutions for charity organisations, teams are
meant to work together. By putting participants in touch with mentors and
nonprofit partners, it fosters technological innovation for social good.

Eligibility Criteria:
0. Degrees: B.Tech./B.E.
1.
Streams or Specializations: Computer Science/ Information
Technology
2. Minimum aggregate 8.5 CGPA [up to the registration
deadline, our results for the third semester are not available,
therefore we filled out our Diploma percentage converted
into CGPA and regulars applied using the CGPA from the
second semester].
Timeline:
➢Registration Process: 10th March to 23rd March
➢Online Coding Test: This time they’ve sent links to students in batches. Mine
was in the 2nd one. Duration was 5th April to 8th April.
➢Video Interview: Deadline 22nd April
➢Code for Good Shortlist announcement: 29th May
➢Code for Good Event: 15th and 16th June
➢Internship Shortlist announcement: 27th August
Online Coding Test (60 minutes):
The
first
phase in the SEP selection process is the online coding test
administered on the HackerRank platform.
There are two programming questions in this 100-point test, both worth 50
marks.
This test has a 60-minute time limit.
The questions I was asked during the coding round were as follows:

1. Minimum servers with maximum load:
It took me ten to fifteen minutes to figure out the solution. I was able to complete
every test case. To be honest, it was a greedy problem that could be solved with
some observation and insight rather than any knowledge of DSA. Try it out before
reading my method.
I was given the projected load and vector capacity of 'n' servers.
I have to find out how many servers are needed to handle the anticipated load.
The bare minimum of severs should be used.
My Approach:
The question was quite simple, but in an attempt to mislead the candidate, a very
long description was provided. However, based on my observations, I discovered
that it is really just a greed issue, similar to the knapsack dilemma.
So I first sort the severs array in ascending order and then start the loop from the
back of the array. Each time I check if current server capacity is smaller than or
equal to current expected load or if expected load - current server capacity is >=
0 to ensure we are choosing correct server. If any of these conditions are met
then we decrement that server capacity from the expected load & increment the
counter to keep track of the servers used.
Explanation with Eg:
Input:
servers = [4, 12, 10, 14, 6]
expected_load = 32
Output:
3
In this case, after sorting, the array will look like: [4, 6, 10, 12, 14]
Now we start from the last element of array so
first we take 14, hence 32 - 14 = 18
Then we take 12 as it is <= 18, 18 - 12 = 6
Now we skip 10 as it is > 6
At last we take 6.

Hence count = 3
2. Parsing the HTTP request:
I don’t remember this problem exactly. The problem involves parsing an array of
HTTP requests (URLs) and extracting tokens and other parameters. The goal is to
validate the "token" parameter against a set of known valid tokens and, for
non-GET requests, check the "csrf" parameter for a minimum length of 8
characters.
If
both conditions are met, the request is considered "VALID."
Otherwise, it is marked "INVALID." Since it was heavily based on strings, I coded it in
Python.
Video Interview (10 minutes):
The next step of the recruiting process is a video interview, powered by HireVue.
In this HireVue interview, you will be asked to record video responses to 2
interview questions.
The types of questions in video interviews are pretty standard and repeated with
most of the candidates, some of them are:
1.
What is your biggest achievement till now, and what learning did you get
from the same?
2. Talk about a recent instance where your friend required assistance to
comprehend a subject that you found to be clear. How will you teach him,
please?
3. When did you change your communication approach with a teammate or
colleague? What was the outcome ?
4. When was your last successful presentation or speech? What was the
subject? What made it successful?
Pretty
standard
questions.
I chose to talk about my recent hackathon
experience
in questions related to my experiences and communication
approach . You can google or search on YouTube ‘HireVue questions’ and you’ll

get a list of questions and good answers for the same.
Also,, there is an option to re-record your response once for each question. If
you re-record any response, that will be automatically submitted as the final
response for that question.
Link to practice: HireVue Digital Interviews
Shortlist Results for CFG:
The final list of all shortlisted students came out about a month later from
the
video
interview
submission,
13 students were selected for the
hackathon.
Code for Good 2024 Hackathon (15th and 16th)
The hackathon for my batch was conducted offline. We’re the first batch to
experience it in the office.
Pre-hackathon Arrangements:
The event was larger than we can think of it as students from all over the country
will be coming for the hackathon at the JPMC’s Mumbai office. 1 week before the
actual hackathon, we’ve got link for the Slack channel to join. 4 days before the
hackathon, we got the list of teams that they have formed over all the students.
Surprisingly, me and my classmate Paras Churi (Noogler 🌚) were on the same
team. Thus, I am content and at ease. There were seven people in the team. Our
team have students from NIT, IIT's, etc.
During hackathon:
Introduction and assignment of problems:
Everyone reached JPMC’s Mumbai office in Goregoan on 15th June. We all VJTIans
then met our team members and had lunch with them. Then the event kicked off
with an introduction to the company. They talked about the company overview,
mission and vision, core values and culture, industry position, and career

development and growth opportunities, employee benefits and perks, and social
initiatives taken up by JPMC. It would be advisable to not skip this since there
might be questions regarding the company in one-on-one with the mentors.
After that, the CFG coordinators introduced the non-profit organisations, their
problem statements, and requirements to all the participants. Following these
presentations, all teams were given time to discuss their order of preference for
the problem statements.
A form was then made available, requiring us to indicate our preferences. The
Assignment of problem statements to each group was done on a first-come,
first-serve basis according to the order of form submissions. (Be very quick while
selecting it. We’ve only got the 2nd topic.)
Then one meeting with the leader of non-profit organisations was scheduled with
all the teams of that problem statement, where every team asked the questions
regarding the problem statement. Make sure you ask the questions and get your
doubts clear before working on the actual project.Also be selfless and never ever
try to defame any teammate or disrespect them. Maintain a very positive attitude
and try to help others going out of your comfort zone.
Setup and Actual Coding:
Then we went to the desks where actual JPMC employees sit and work. We were
assigned 2 mentors whom with we discussed the problem statement. They first
asked us to introduce ourselves and asked about our hobbies.
We've been assigned to solve the problem for the EAGL Livelihood Foundation,
which is the NGO that works for the tribal communities, where they wanted to
digitalise the data related operations and tracking system.
We then started brainstorming about the problem. During this brainstorming,
make sure to express your thoughts in front of the mentors, as it’s the most
important factor that will decide your selection also. Trust me, one girl from our
team has got the offer who has done nothing in development and only made the
final PPT 😂. But one thing she has done is expressed her thoughts while making
the flow of the project in front of mentors. Meanwhile, I’ve done backend
authentication in both MySQL & MongoDB, payment integration etc. one day
before the hackathon 😂.

We built the workflow of the entire project and then divided the work among our
team. There are 2 girls in the team, we’ve divided the work as follows:
●
2 girls and 1 boy: Frontend for the application
●
Paras, me and 1 guy: Entire Backend
●
One guy: Python with OpenCV for parsing.
Out of which other 2 were done except the first one, as they don’t know the
frontend very much. So I decided to use the UI of one of the projects for this one
(this is how your project helps you in such situations) and then refined and
integrated it with the backend. Be prepare to take control of whatever technology
you’ve worked before. I’ve taken care of the frontend and entire version control
system, as many of the team members don’t even know how git works.
During this process we got to enjoy very much as there are snacks, are available
24 * 7. The dinner and lunch were also very delicious. There are some activities at
midnight in the office where some coordinators try to relax us by singing the song
or asking any of the students to perform anything they want. Our mentors were
also very supportive and friendly, and they continuously guided us throughout
our development.
Evaluation:
The next day, at 10 am, we stopped working. It was time for an assessment now.
Several committees are assessing the various teams at the same time. We have
10 to 15 minutes to address their questions about our implementation and to
outline our strategy for the project. Next, we received a CFG bag and the
hackathon certificate. Then, in the afternoon, all teams are brought together at
the conference hall. Subsequently, they declare the top three teams for each
problem statement. Unfortunately, we are not qualified. However, it has no impact
on the employment procedure. The top three teams then presented their ideas to
each of the non-profit organisations, and one of them was chosen as the winner.
Since we had been awake for more than twenty-four hours, everyone was literally
exhausted at that point.
There was no one-on-one mentoring round with our team members. Although
some of my friends in other teams have undergone the one-on-one discussion
with the mentor.

My tips for the hackathon:
●
Take initiative, do not wait for others to mess something up and then tell
them.
●
Be quick and prompt in decision making, and split work according to the
skillset of members.
●
Voice
your
opinions
clearly,
and make sure there is constant
communication between ALL team members. This is the most crucial
piece of advice.
●
Always support & help your team and put your team first.
●
Regularly give suggestions and have conversations with team to
regularly track the progress, replan and then motivate teammates.
●
You do not need to win the hackathon in order to secure an internship.
You may not get an internship even if you win the hackathon. But you
need to show throughout the hackathon that you are a good team
player, and developer.
We did not win the hackathon, but 4 out of 7 of my teammates (including
me) secured an internship, and this is only because our teamwork was
incredibly smooth, and we had effective communication and collaboration.
Internship Offer
After 2 months, the internship selections were announced, 3 out of 13
received internship offers, and all 3 accepted the offer.

Tips (In general):
Even though I did not have a conventional interview like most do, I did keep
working on myself for 2 months, like preparing the CS fundamentals, practicing
DSA, and solving puzzles, etc. until I got the internship offer. So these tips are not
exactly just limited to JPMC but for internship interviews in general.
●
Practice DSA from sites like Leetcode and GFG. Personally, I only used
Leetcode because of the better interface and community)
●
Solve problems from lists – there are many, but choose one that suits you.
●
Some examples are Strivers SDE sheet, Neetcode 150 etc. Personally, I used
Strivers A2Z DSA sheet, which is next level.
●
Practice OOPS from sites like GFG & Javatpoint.
●
Practice DBMS and OS from your academic notes/presentations. They are
more than enough for your interviews.
●
You can practice the interview questions for any CS fundamentals &
development technology related topics from here:
https://www.interviewbit.com/
Final advice
The preparation phase can indeed be overwhelming and exhausting, both
mentally and physically. It's important to prioritise your health and mental
well-being during this time. Stress is a common experience, and every batch
goes through it—including myself. Remember, this is a journey to be enjoyed,
not just endured. Stay happy and take care of yourself along the way!
All the best! Cheers!
